idiom_name: plain class for lifecycle owners + frozen dataclasses for values
implementation_notes: Python binds behaviour to data with ordinary classes, but nothing enforces encapsulation: the idiomatic realization is a plain class with _private attributes, read-only @property accessors and intent-named methods for entities that own a lifecycle, @dataclass(frozen=True) for value objects (generated init/eq/repr plus validation in __post_init__), and module-level functions for behaviour that needs no object. The rich class remains justified for aggregates and state machines; the anemic trap in Python is a mutable dataclass with public fields while the rules live in a service module.
pitfalls: The underscore convention is the only encapsulation; ORMs, serializers and test code can still write order._lines - expose read-only properties and rebuild state through methods.
Mutable class attributes or mutable default arguments are shared between instances and silently break invariants; initialise per instance in __init__.
@dataclass generates value equality; for identity-bearing objects, use eq=False and compare by id, otherwise a reloaded entity equals a different one.
